newsitem.title: FRANCE: French drugs shares supported by market rumours.
newsitem.headline: French drugs shares supported by market rumours.

text.p: French pharmaceutical shares were higher on Thursday supported by a newspaper article on possible buys by Pharmacia-Upjohn in France as well as other rumours, dealers said.
The Les Echos financial newspaper said that, one year after its merger, Pharmacia-Upjohn was looking for acquisitions in France and Germany.
At 1319 GMT, Rousell-Uclaf was 3.72 percent higher at 1,227 francs, Synthelabo was up 3.19 percent at 474.80 and Sanofi traded 0.77 percent higher at 455.50.
Roussel-Uclaf is controlled by Hoechst of Germany and Sanofi by Elf-Aquitaine.
"We are studying a number of projects which could be concluded between now and a year," Les Echos quoted Sven Andreasson, chairman of Pharmacia-Upjohn France, as saying.
Dealers also noted London stock market rumours that Switzerland's Roche Holdings would make a bid for Zeneca, which boosted the sector.
"The rumour of a Roche bid for Zeneca is an old chesnut that comes back regularly, but it keeps investors interested," a dealer said.
Roussel-Uclaf was further underpinned by renewed speculation that Hoescht might buy out minority holders ahead a big restructuring of drugs activities within Hoescht Marion Roussel.
Synthelabo was helped by speculation it could replace Thomson-CSF in the CAC-40 after a possible buy-out bid by Lagardere.
